opus-5.5.text:
I think I should be honest that a lot of what I said today is just my personal view, shaped by my own experience at a particular moment. The field moves so fast that some of these opinions may already look outdated in six months, and some may simply be wrong. I've tried to share what I actually believe rather than what sounds good, but I hold these views fairly loosely.

If I had to sum it up, I'm most confident about the things that come from direct, hands-on experience: what it feels like to train models, to see experiments fail, and to work with a small team that really cares about getting things right. I'm less confident about predictions, such as where the technology is going, timelines, or what the industry will look like. Those are guesses, and I'd encourage listeners to treat them that way.

I also hope people don't take any single sentence out of context. Many of these questions don't have clean answers, and the nuance matters. If anything I said makes someone think more carefully, or even disagree and go test it themselves, that would make me happiest. In the end, the results will speak more clearly than any of us can in an interview.

r001.rationale: The candidate says some interview opinions may look outdated in six months or simply be wrong, conveying that Luo expects some of these views may later prove incorrect.

fable-5.1.text:
Honestly, I'd ask people to treat everything I've said today as a snapshot, not a conclusion. The field is moving so fast that some of what I believe right now about model training, about where open source is heading, about how far we are from truly general systems, I'll probably look back on in a year and find partly wrong. That's not false modesty. When I think about the views I held two or three years ago, a good share of them didn't survive contact with what actually happened.

What I do stand behind is the way of thinking rather than the specific predictions. I try to reason from first principles about what the data and compute actually allow, rather than from what the narrative of the moment says. I try to be honest about what we don't understand yet, because in this field pretending to certainty is one of the fastest ways to make bad decisions. And I care a lot about the people doing the work, because in the end, research culture decides which problems get taken seriously.

So if listeners take anything away, I'd rather it be a set of questions to keep asking than a set of answers from me. The answers will change. The questions, hopefully, are the durable part.

r001.rationale: The candidate says they will probably look back in a year and find some of today’s views partly wrong.

astra-6.text: I’d treat them as provisional judgments rather than definitive conclusions. I may be missing context, and my own experience inevitably shapes how I see things. I’m happy to revise my views when there’s good reason to do so.

r001.rationale: The candidate says the views are provisional and open to revision, but does not convey an expectation that Fuli Luo will later judge them to be wrong.
